changes_needed
The revised leakage check also masks timestamps, so target-hour lookup can still fail.
Checks: 29 tests passed; link checker reports bad 0. External sources were not checked offline.

findings.checklist_item: Accuracy: code sketches must do what the text says
findings.title: Preserve timestamp labels when masking unavailable measurements
findings.claim: The correction masks every column in an unavailable row, including timestamp. Keeping rows therefore does not guarantee that target-hour labels survive. A feature that builds its time index from the exercise's timestamp column still loses those labels and raises at .loc[target_hours].
findings.evidence: Line 711 passes df.where(df.available_at <= issue_time) to feature_fn. The exercise supplies timestamp as a column. For a feature implemented as frame.set_index('timestamp')['actual_mw'].shift(24), unavailable target timestamps become NaT before indexing, so the requested target hours are absent. This is a new problem in the replacement proposed for PR43-F5. Checked by reading; pandas is unavailable here, so this example was not executed.
findings.proposed_change: Clarify that timestamps form a fixed target grid. Preserve that grid and availability metadata, and mask only measurement columns such as actual_mw. Add a regression example using a timestamp column and a 24-hour lag: target lookup must succeed, with available lag values retained and unavailable values marked missing.
